st.2: Kotada is the local name of Dholavira.

x: All three are correct: Mohenjodaro means "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi (Lothal means the same in Gujarati), Kotada is the local name of Dholavira, and Kalibangan means "black bangles".
All three are correct: the second Dilmun temple on Failaka (Nov 2025), Dilmun weights on the Harappan standard, and contacts with Altyn-depe (also Shahr-i-Sokhta and Tepe Yahya).

st.1: It is a steatite seal found at Mohenjodaro.

x: All three are correct: the steatite Pashupati seal was found at Mohenjodaro; its three-faced horned figure sits in a yogic posture, surrounded by elephant, tiger, rhinoceros and buffalo, with two deer below the seat.

st.3: People lived mainly in villages, as the large planned cities had declined.

x: All three are correct: the Late Harappan phase (c. 1900–1300 BCE) was post-urban – people lived mainly in villages – though burnt bricks were still used at Bhagwanpura in Haryana.
Both are correct: the Ghaggar-Hakra had the densest cluster of sites before it dried, and Chanhudaro was flooded several times.

st.2: Women were excluded from the assemblies in the Later Vedic period.

x: Both are correct: women attended the Sabha (Sabhavati) and the Vidatha in early Vedic times but were excluded in the Later Vedic period.

st.1: The Puranas are classed as Shruti.

x: 2 and 3 are correct: the Aranyakas and Upanishads form the Jnana-kanda, and the Atharvaveda has no Aranyaka. 1 is wrong: the Puranas are Smriti, not Shruti (Shruti = the Vedic Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads).

st.2: The Battle of Ten Kings is described in Mandala VII.

x: All four are correct: the family books (II–VII) are the oldest core, the Battle of Ten Kings is in Mandala VII, the Nasadiya Sukta is in Mandala X, and 30 Rigveda manuscripts at BORI, Pune are on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.

st.2: The Dhamek stupa at Sarnath, of the Gupta period, marks the Buddha's enlightenment.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Dhamek stupa at Sarnath marks the Buddha's first sermon (Dharmachakra-pravartana), not his enlightenment, which was at Bodh Gaya.

st.3: He divided society into seven classes, one of which was the philosophers.

x: All four are correct: Pataliputra's wooden palisade had 64 gates and 570 towers, the city was run by six committees of five members, the town officials were Astynomoi, and philosophers headed his seven classes (merchants were not one of them).

st.3: Ujjain was the capital of Dakshinapatha.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Ujjain was the capital of Avantipatha; Dakshinapatha's capital was Suvarnagiri.

st.3: The Bharhut stupa was found by Alexander Cunningham.

x: All three are correct: Sanchi is in Raisen district near Vidisha, Stupa No. 3 holds the relics of Sariputta and Mahamoggallana, and Bharhut (Satna, MP; Sunga, c. 150 BCE) was found by Alexander Cunningham (Colin Mackenzie traced Amaravati in 1797).

st.2: Devagrahara grants were made to temples and monasteries for worship.
st.3: The earliest land grants in India were made by the Mauryas.

x: 1 and 2 are correct: brahmadeya grants went to Brahmanas with tax exemption and administrative rights, and devagrahara / devadana grants went to temples and monasteries. 3 is wrong: the earliest land grants were made by the Satavahanas in the Deccan, not the Mauryas.

st.2: His account is known as the Fo-kwo-ki.
st.3: He visited India during the reign of Kumaragupta I.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct: he came overland and returned by sea via Sri Lanka, his account is the Fo-kwo-ki, and he saw 20 viharas at Mathura. 3 is wrong: he came c. 399–412 CE under Chandragupta II, not Kumaragupta I.

st.2: The Eastern Chalukya queens Ayyana Mahadevi and Chamakamba are known as temple builders.

x: Both are correct: the Kalyani Chalukya princess Akkadevi governed Kisukad, and the Eastern Chalukya queens Ayyana Mahadevi and Chamakamba were temple builders (not governors).

st.1: The village was divided into 30 wards (kudumbus).
st.4: A person who had served in the previous three years was not barred from being chosen again.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct: 30 wards (kudumbus), palm-leaf lots drawn in public by a young boy, and a 360-day term. 4 is wrong: anyone who had served in the previous three years was barred.

st.1: He crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290 at about the age of 70.
st.3: He married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Timur.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct: he crowned himself at Kilokhari (1290) at about 70, was lenient to rebels like Malik Chhajju, and Mongol converts were settled as 'New Mussalmans'. 3 is wrong: Ulugh Khan was a descendant of Chengiz Khan, not Timur.

st.2: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah, the last Khalji, was murdered by Malik Kafur.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Kafur himself was killed; Mubarak Shah was murdered by Khusrau Khan (Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah).

st.3: Alauddin's price controls were abolished by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20), not Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, abolished the price control and restored the confiscated lands.

st.1: Barani wrote the Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Barani wrote the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari; the Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is Firoz's own account.

st.2: The Kulah-daran were the ulema.

x: 1 is correct: the Ajlaf were lower-status Muslims. 2 is wrong: the Kulah-daran were the Sayyids; the ulema were the Dastar-bandan.

st.1: Dara Shikoh's siege of 1653 failed to recover Kandahar for the Mughals.

x: All three are correct: Ali Mardan Khan surrendered Kandahar in 1638, Persia (Shah Abbas II) took it back in 1649, and Aurangzeb's sieges (1649, 1652) and Dara's siege (1653) all failed, so Kandahar was lost for good.

st.2: In the First Battle of Tarain (1191) Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan.

x: 1 and 3 are correct: Mahmud's 17 raids (1000-1027) and Timur's sack of Delhi (1398). 2 is wrong: Ghori was defeated by Prithviraj Chauhan at Tarain I (1191) and won only at Tarain II (1192).
All three are correct: Armenians were among the Asian merchants, Europeans paid mainly in bullion, and the trade balance favoured India till the mid-18th century.

st.2: He abolished the pilgrim tax (1563) and the jizya (1564), and neither was ever reimposed by his successors.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct; noble households stayed full of slaves despite the 1562 measure. 2 is wrong: though Akbar abolished the pilgrim tax (1563) and jizya (1564), Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya in 1679.

st.2: Sepoys were trained in the new rifle at Meerut, Lucknow and Kanpur.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: training in the Enfield rifle was held at Dum Dum, Ambala and Sialkot, not Meerut, Lucknow and Kanpur.

st.3: European troops in India had been drawn off for the Crimean and Afghan wars.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: European troops had been drawn off for the Crimean and Persian wars, not the Afghan wars.

st.4: Chandurti is to British rule in Andhra what Plassey is to British rule in India.

x: All four are correct: Chandurti (near Rajahmundry, 1758), "a small battle with great results" (Malleson), drove the French out of the Northern Circars, and it founded British rule in Andhra as Plassey did in India.

st.2: The Treaty of Mangalore (March 1784) that ended the Second war was concluded with Haidar Ali.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Haidar Ali died on 7 December 1782; the Treaty of Mangalore (1784) was made with Tipu Sultan.

st.2: The Second war followed Holkar's victory over the Peshwa and Sindhia at Hadapsar near Poona in 1802.

x: All three are correct: Salbai (May 1782) ended the First war; at Hadapsar (Oct 1802) Holkar beat the Peshwa and Sindhia, Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein and the Second war followed; the Peshwaship was abolished in June 1818.

st.3: The states kept control of their internal administration.

x: All three are correct: Rajputana states such as Udaipur, Jaipur and Jodhpur gave up external relations for British protection but kept internal administration.

st.4: The Arms Act of 1878 was passed during the viceroyalty of Ripon.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the Arms Act and the Vernacular Press Act (both 1878) were Lytton's; Ripon repealed the VPA in 1882.

st.3: Peshkash was the fixed payment of zamindars, not a name for its common ownership.

x: All three are correct: common ownership under the Mahalwari system was called Bhai Chara or Mahali, while Peshkash was the fixed payment of zamindars.

st.3: The higher ratio made Indian goods dearer abroad.

x: All four are correct: the rupee was fixed at 1s 6d, Indian business under Purshottamdas Thakurdas wanted 1s 4d, the higher ratio made Indian goods dearer abroad (hurting exporters), and the central-bank recommendation led to the RBI in 1935.
All three are correct: Osmania – Mir Osman Ali Khan, Urdu medium; SV University – Tirupati 1954 (CM T. Prakasam); the Deccan Education Society (1884) founded Fergusson College in 1885.

st.2: It was issued when Lord Dalhousie was the Governor-General.

x: All three are correct: Sir Charles Wood issued it on 19 July 1854 under Lord Dalhousie (1835 = Bentinck + Macaulay; 1854 = Wood + Dalhousie), and it laid down the graded hierarchy from vernacular primary schools to universities.

st.1: The Sati Regulation (XVII of 1829) was passed under Lord Dalhousie.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Sati Regulation (1829) was William Bentinck's, not Dalhousie's (abetment = culpable homicide).

st.2: Dayananda wrote Satyarth Prakash in Hindi.
st.3: Dayananda founded the Arya Samaj at Lahore in 1875.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Satyarth Prakash ('The Light of Truth', 1875) was written in Hindi, and the Samaj set 25 and 16 as minimum marriage ages. 3 is wrong: the Arya Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1875 (its ten principles were finalised at Lahore in 1877).

st.3: Its organ Rast Goftar was edited by Behramji Malabari.

x: 1 and 2 are correct: the Sabha promoted girls' education and marriage reform. 3 is wrong: Rast Goftar was edited by Dadabhai Naoroji, not Malabari.

st.3: The English paper Crescent (Madras, 1844) was founded by Gazula Lakshminarasu Chetty.

x: All three are correct: The Hindu (Triplicane Six, weekly 1878, daily 1889), the Telugu Swarajya of Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, and The Crescent (1844) of Gazula Lakshminarasu Chetty.

st.2: The name 'Indian National Congress' was suggested by Dadabhai Naoroji.

x: All four are correct: Hume's Indian National Union (1884) became the INC, the name was suggested by Dadabhai Naoroji (W.C. Bonnerjee was the first President), 17 people met after the Theosophical Convention, and the Indian National Conference merged in 1886.
Both are correct: Bismil was born on 11 June 1897 and Sukhdev on 15 May 1907 at Ludhiana.

st.2: Its demand was two-thirds of the crop for the bargadar.

x: All four are correct: the Bengal Provincial Kisan Sabha called it (Sept 1946) to implement the Floud Commission, tebhaga meant two-thirds of the crop for the bargadar, bargadars fought jotedars, and it led to the Bargadari Act (1950).

st.3: Shanti Ghosh was a martyr of the Quit India Movement in Comilla.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Shanti Ghosh was a revolutionary of 1931 (Comilla) and is not linked to Quit India.

st.1: The parallel government at Satara was the longest-lasting of them.

x: All three are correct: Satara (mid-1943 to 1945/46) was the longest-lasting (Ballia lasted only about a week), with Nyayadan Mandals and village libraries, and the Jatiya Sarkar of Tamluk ran Vidyut Vahinis and cyclone relief.

st.3: Mountbatten, told to keep India united if possible, came as Viceroy in succession to Lord Linlithgow.

x: 1 and 2 are correct: the 30 June 1948 deadline, and power possibly to provincial governments (a hint of Balkanisation). 3 is wrong: Mountbatten succeeded Lord Wavell (March 1947), not Linlithgow.

st.2: He took his M.A. (Hons) in Economics from Edinburgh in 1916.

x: All four are correct: born at Penuganchiprolu, M.A. (Hons) in Economics at Edinburgh (1916), introduced to Gandhi by Coomaraswamy, and later an Andhra secretary of the Swaraj Party.

st.2: Prakasam's Khadi Centre at Guravareddypalem received Rs 10,000 from the All India Spinners' Association.
st.3: Heavy industrialisation was an item of Gandhi's constructive programme.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Ponduru khadi, the Rs 10,000 from the All India Spinners' Association, and khadi for rural self-reliance. 3 is wrong: the constructive programme comprised khadi, prohibition, removal of untouchability, national schools, Hindu-Muslim unity and village panchayats – not heavy industrialisation.

st.1: Bhimavaram, where police fired on 17 August, is in West Godavari district.

x: All three are correct: police fired at Bhimavaram (West Godavari) on 17 August, Kakinada lawyers demanded Gandhi's release, and Bapatla railway station was burnt.

st.3: It was chaired by Chief Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.

x: 1 and 2 are correct: set up in December 2004, it made 104 recommendations. 3 is wrong: it was chaired by Minister Koneru Ranga Rao, not P.V. Narasimha Rao.

st.3: Konda Venkatappayya was the secretary of the committee formed to organise an all-Andhra conference.

x: All three are correct: Nidadavolu (May 1912) was a joint Godavari-Krishna-Guntur conference, Jonnavittula Gurunatham's resolution was ruled out of order, and Konda Venkatappayya was the committee's secretary (Nyapati Subba Rao opposed a separate province in 1912).

All three are correct: the Guntur special session (1918) protested the Montford proposals, Pattabhi proposed an All-India Linguistic States Conference, and the Nandyal session (1928, presided over by S. Radhakrishnan) renamed the Ceded districts Rayalaseema.

st.3: Sir Vijaya, president of the Mahasabha, met Stafford Cripps on 2 April 1942.

x: All three are correct: the Madras special session (1931) under Kadapa Koti Reddy, the Rayalaseema safeguards at the Silver Jubilee session (1937), and Sir Vijaya (president 1941-46) meeting Cripps on 2 April 1942 during the Cripps Mission.

st.2: The Andhra Assembly passed Bezawada Gopala Reddy's merger resolution of 1955 unanimously.

x: All three are correct: the Hyderabad Assembly vote (103 for, 29 against, 15 neutral), the Andhra Assembly's unanimous passing of the resolution, and the 1956 Delhi talks with leaders of both regions.

st.2: K.V. Ranga Reddy changed sides, while Marri Chenna Reddy opposed Visalandhra throughout.

x: All three are correct: Kaloji first supported and later opposed Visalandhra, K.V. Ranga Reddy changed sides while Chenna Reddy opposed throughout, and Makhdoom Mohiuddin was among the educated Muslims who supported it.

st.1: Bhumaka and Nahapana belonged to the Kshaharata line.

x: All three are correct: Abhiraka, Bhumaka and Nahapana were Kshaharatas (Nasik-Junnar-Karle), while Chashtana and Rudradaman I were Kardamakas (Ujjain, Malwa, Kathiawar).

st.3: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi was the 23rd king of the list.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 23rd king was Gautamiputra Satakarni, the last of the early Satavahanas; Vasishthiputra Pulumavi was the 24th.

st.2: Roman trade declined after the Satavahanas.

x: Both are correct: Roman trade peaked in the Satavahana period (1st c. BCE-3rd c. CE) and declined after them.

st.3: The pot of 3,730 lead coins found in 2024 came from Phanigiri, not Thotlakonda.

x: All three are correct: Thotlakonda was spotted by an Indian Navy aerial survey, its 1988–92 digs found Satavahana and Roman coins, and the 3,730 lead coins (2024) come from Phanigiri.

st.3: The Vishnukundins bore the titles Paramamaheswara and Parama Brahmanya.

x: All three are correct: the Amaravati reliefs show naga, yaksha and tree worship, Sriparvataswamy was the Vishnukundin family deity, and their titles were Paramamaheswara and Parama Brahmanya.

st.2: The Varada mudra shows a lowered open palm.

x: All three are correct: in Bhumisparsha the earth is called to witness, Varada is a lowered open (boon-giving) palm, and Abhaya (raised right palm) is linked with subduing Nalagiri.

st.3: Santamula's daughter Adavi Santisri married Skanda Visakha of the Dhanika family.

x: All three are correct: Virapurushadatta married Bapisri and Shastisri, his daughter Kodabalisri married the Chutu king, and Adavi Santisri married Skanda Visakha of the Dhanikas (Santamula's sister Santisri married Skandasri of the Pugiyas).

st.1: They were mainly of gold and silver.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: Ikshvaku coins were of lead and copper, not gold and silver; they are found in Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts.

st.3: None of the four shares of revenue went to overseas colonies.

x: All three are correct: revenue went to tanks and canals, the age shifted to an agrarian agrahara order, and the four shares were administration and army; temples and festivals; poets and scholars; gifts to religious bodies – none to colonies.

st.2: Ehuvala's Gummadidurru record is in Prakrit.
st.3: Prakrit replaced Sanskrit in the inscriptions from the 4th century CE.

x: 1 and 2 are correct: Swarna Devalayam is the first Sanskrit inscription of South India, and the Gummadidurru record is in Prakrit. 3 is wrong: the shift was the other way – Sanskrit replaced Prakrit from the 4th century CE.

st.3: Of their eight inscriptions, five are in Sanskrit.

x: All four are correct: Vijaya Devavarma's Ashvamedha, Hastivarma's defeat by Samudragupta, five of eight inscriptions in Sanskrit (three Prakrit – Sanskrit replaced Prakrit from their time), and Madhava Varma II's conquest of Vengi.

st.2: The Ipur plates, with Lakshmi and conch symbols, belong to Madhava Varma I.

x: All four are correct: Chikkulla's Telugu phrase, the Ipur plates of Madhava Varma I, the divine ordeals of the Polamuru plates and the Tummalagudem grant of Govinda Varma I.

st.3: Early multi-armed metal images made by the lost-wax method are credited to the Vishnukundin age.

x: All three are correct: the Vishnukundin cave temples (4th-6th c.) mix Ikshvaku and Vakataka traditions, Keesaragutta has brick structural temples, and the early lost-wax multi-armed metal images are Vishnukundin.

st.1: The Addanki inscription of Pandaranga, in the Taruvoja metre, is the first Telugu poetic inscription.

x: All four are correct: Addanki (Pandaranga, Taruvoja) is the first poetic inscription (Pitikayagulla only shows post-Badami Chalukya script influence), Bhattiprolu is Prakrit in Brahmi, the Old Kannada-Telugu script was shared, and the rounded Telugu script came in the 11th-14th centuries.

st.2: He used the Akkara metre, borrowed from Tamil.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Nannaya borrowed the Akkara metre from Kannada, not Tamil.

st.3: Anavota Reddy shifted the Reddi capital from Addanki to Kondavidu.

x: All three are correct: the Kakatiyas became sovereign in 1163 and moved to Orugallu, Penugonda and Chandragiri were later Vijayanagara capitals, and Anavota Reddy moved the Reddi capital to Kondavidu (Prolaya Vemareddy was the founder).

st.2: In 1323 Prataparudra was captured by Ulugh Khan.

x: All three are correct: Kafur made Prataparudra a tributary (1309–10), Ulugh Khan (later Muhammad bin Tughlaq) captured him in 1323, and the unifiers of the Telugu lands were the Satavahanas, Kakatiyas and Qutb Shahis.

st.3: The Kakatiya conflict with the Yadavas (Sevunas) began under Prola II.

x: All four are correct: the Kampili tradition of Harihara and Bukka, the Nayankara system carried on by Vijayanagara, the Yadava conflict beginning under Prola II, and Rudramadevi's repulse of Mahadeva.

st.3: The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam of 1416 was issued by the Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya I.

x: All three are correct: the Motupalli charter is the chief Kakatiya commercial document, sandal, camphor, rose-water and ivory were traded there, and the 1416 Dharma Sasanam belongs to Deva Raya I.

st.2: The Nayankaras held about one-fourth of the land of the kingdom.

x: All four are correct: Nayakasthalam villages instead of salary, about one-fourth of the land (one-sixth was the usual land-revenue rate), revenue and army duties with a fixed annual payment, and Ekamranatha's Pratapa Charitra as a source.

st.2: Kondapalli was taken after Kandukuru, Vinukonda and Kondaveedu.
st.4: Cuttack and the Gajapati heartland were annexed to Vijayanagara under the peace.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Udayagiri fell after an 18-month siege, Kondapalli and Bejawada came after Kandukuru, Vinukonda, Addanki and Kondaveedu, and Annapurna Devi married Krishnadevaraya. 4 is wrong: Cuttack was not annexed – lands north of the Krishna were returned to the Gajapati.
All three are correct: Dilawar Khan Ghuri (1401, Dhar) founded the Sultanate, Hoshang Shah shifted to Mandu, and the Hindola Mahal is the T-shaped 'swinging palace' with sloping walls.

st.2: Ramarajabhushana (Bhattumurti) dedicated his Vasucharitramu to Tirumala Raya.

x: All three are correct: Nandi Timmana (Mukku Timmana) wrote Parijatapaharanamu, Bhattumurti dedicated Vasucharitramu to Tirumala Raya (not Achyutaraya), and Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu wrote Ramabhyudayamu.

st.3: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794.

x: All three are correct: Vizianagaram became a zamindari estate in 1802, the Vatsavayis ruled from Peddapuram, and the Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794.

st.3: Vijayaditya II is credited with building 108 temples.
st.4: They were in a pure Vesara style based on Hoysala models.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Dravidian idiom from Pallava and Badami Chalukya forms, laterite and limestone, and the 108 temples of Vijayaditya II. 4 is wrong: 'pure Vesara on Hoysala models' is the trap – they were Dravidian.

st.1: In 1808 they were split into the collectorates of Bellary and Cuddapah.

x: All three are correct: the 1808 split created the Bellary and Cuddapah collectorates (till then one collectorate at Anantapur), the districts were Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary, and the old name was Dattamandalam.

st.3: The Treaty of Aurangabad (1753), part of the background, had given the Circars to the French.

x: All four are correct: Ranga Rao defended Bobbili against Vijayarama Raju and Bussy, Tandra Paparayudu killed Vijayarama Raju, the Treaty of Aurangabad (1753) gave the Circars to the French, and it was during the Third Carnatic War.

st.2: The Viswa Sahityamala was run by the Mahidhara brothers.

x: All four are correct: Krovvidi Lingaraju's Amma (1934), the Mahidhara brothers' Viswa Sahityamala (Gadde Lingayya ran the Adarsha Grantha Mandali), Gopichand's Sahitya Akademi award and his post as first Director of Information (1953).

st.2: She received the Padma Vibhushan in 1975.

x: All three are correct: she was a Constituent Assembly member, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1975 and founded the Andhra Aatmiya Sabha.

st.3: By 1905 there were about twenty Telugu journals in circulation.

x: All three are correct: Andhra Prakasika (1885) was the first political Telugu weekly, Purushartha Pradayini carried views for and against widow remarriage, and by 1905 there were about 20 Telugu journals.

st.2: Article 243D(3) applies to Panchayats, and Article 243T(3) to Municipalities.

x: Both are correct: the 73rd/74th Amendments (1992) gave one-third seats to women – Article 243D(3) for Panchayats and 243T(3) for Municipalities.
Both are correct: the anti-arrack movement began in Dubagunta, Nellore, and was led by rural women.

st.3: Kalashoka made Rajgriha the permanent capital.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Kalashoka moved the capital back to Pataliputra, not Rajgriha; it stayed the capital of the Mauryas and Guptas.

st.3: The Nanda army was huge, and fear of it made Alexander's soldiers refuse to march beyond the Beas.

x: All three are correct: Dhana Nanda (Agrammes) was Alexander's contemporary, Bhaddasala commanded the Nanda army, and the huge Nanda army was a reason Alexander's soldiers refused to go beyond the Beas.

st.2: Heliodorus was the envoy of the Bactrian king Demetrius.
st.4: Its inscription is in the Greek language.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Heliodorus was the envoy of the Indo-Greek king Antialcidas (not Demetrius) to the Sunga king Bhagabhadra. 4 is wrong: the inscription is in Prakrit, in Brahmi, not Greek.

st.3: Uraiyur was the inland Chola capital and a craft centre.

x: All three are correct: Tondi (Tyndis) was a Chera port, Korkai was famed for pearls, and Uraiyur was the inland Chola capital and craft centre, not a port.

st.2: Govinda III was the predecessor of Dhruva.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Govinda III was Dhruva's successor, not his predecessor.

st.2: Sanskrit was their language of scholarship, while they encouraged Marathi, their mother tongue.
st.3: Devagiri was renamed Daulatabad by Alauddin Khalji.

x: 1 and 2 are correct: the Seunas were first Kalyani Chalukya feudatories, and they encouraged Marathi beside Sanskrit. 3 is wrong: Devagiri was renamed Daulatabad by Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1327), not Alauddin Khalji.

st.3: The World Bank (Spring 2025) says the consumption Gini rose from 25.5 in 2011-12 to 28.8 in 2022-23.

x: 1 and 2 are correct: WIR 2026 (top 10% ~65%) and Oxfam (top 1% 40.5% in 2021). 3 is wrong: it reverses the trend – the World Bank shows the consumption Gini falling from 28.8 (2011-12) to 25.5 (2022-23).

st.2: New Delhi hosted the World Social Forum in 2004.

x: 1 and 3 are correct: Porto Alegre 2001 and Seattle 1999 (WTO Ministerial). 2 is wrong: the 2004 World Social Forum was held in Mumbai, not New Delhi.

st.2: Under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 a bigamous marriage is only voidable.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct: levirate (husband's brother; Gond, Munda), fraternal polyandry (Toda, Khasa) and sororate (wife's sister). 2 is wrong: under HMA Section 11 a bigamous marriage is void, not voidable (Section 12 deals with voidable marriages).

st.1: A person has 8 primary kin, all of them blood (consanguineous) relatives.
st.2: The wife's brother and the sister's husband are tertiary kin.
st.4: An uncle is a primary relative.

x: Only 3 is correct: 33 secondary and 151 tertiary kin. 1 is wrong: of the 8 primary kin the spouse is an affinal, not a blood, relative. 2 is wrong: the wife's brother and sister's husband are secondary kin (primary kin of primary kin). 4 is wrong: an uncle is a secondary relative.

st.1: In a village, social control is formal – through law and police.

x: 2 and 3 are correct: town relations are secondary and impersonal, and Redfield's folk-urban continuum came from Yucatan. 1 is wrong: village social control is informal (caste, custom); formal control (law, police) marks the town.

st.2: Both are in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

x: Only 1 is correct: Khasi and Garo are official languages of Meghalaya with English. 2 is wrong: neither is in the Eighth Schedule.

st.2: Operation All Clear (2003) against ULFA was conducted in Myanmar.
st.4: Operation Parakram (2001-02) was launched against Khalistani militants in Punjab.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Operation All Clear (2003) was conducted in Bhutan, not Myanmar. 4 is wrong: Parakram was a troop mobilisation on the Pakistan border, not a Punjab operation (Blue Star, 1984, was the Khalistan operation).

st.2: Danial Latifi (2001) limited a divorced Muslim wife's maintenance to the iddat period.
st.3: Shayara Bano (2017) held instant triple talaq unconstitutional, with Chief Justice J.S. Khehar writing the majority opinion.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Danial Latifi held maintenance extends beyond iddat, for her whole life. 3 is wrong: the 3:2 majority was formed by Justices Nariman, Lalit and Joseph; CJI Khehar (with Justice Nazeer) was in the minority.

st.1: Bhopal became the first officially beggar-free city in 2025.
st.3: In the Census 2011 list of beggars and vagrants, Andhra Pradesh ranks second after West Bengal.

x: Only 2 is correct: SMILE has a sub-scheme for rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging. 1 is wrong: the first officially beggar-free city (2025) was Indore, not Bhopal. 3 is wrong: Uttar Pradesh (65,835) is second after West Bengal (81,224); Andhra Pradesh (30,218) is third.

st.2: AP ranked 11th in India in Crime in India 2023, a report published by the National Investigation Agency.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Crime in India (AP 11th in 2023) is published by the National Crime Records Bureau, not the NIA.

st.1: Secessionist movements such as the Naga, Assam and Khalistan movements are the only form of youth unrest.
st.2: The Dalit Panthers, a militant Dalit youth organisation, were formed in Tamil Nadu in 1972.

x: Only 3 is correct: drug abuse is classed as deviance. 1 is wrong: secessionist movements are one form of youth unrest, not the only one (deviance such as drug abuse is another). 2 is wrong: the Dalit Panthers were formed in Maharashtra (Bombay), 1972.

st.2: The PM-Vidyalaxmi scheme provides education loans only against collateral.
st.3: The APSSDC, a body under the Union Ministry of Skill Development, trained about 2.6 lakh youth in 2024-25.

x: Only 1 is correct: NSS (1969), 'Education through Service'. 2 is wrong: PM-Vidyalaxmi gives collateral-free (and guarantor-free) education loans. 3 is wrong: the APSSDC is Andhra Pradesh's own State Skill Development Corporation, not a Union body.

st.1: Disguised unemployment is mainly found in the urban labour market.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: disguised unemployment is found mainly in agriculture (family farms), not the urban labour market; frictional and educated unemployment are urban.

st.1: India's unemployment rate rose from 3.2% in 2017-18 to 6.1% in 2023-24.
st.3: Andhra Pradesh's labour force participation rate measures only the employed as a share of the population.

x: Only 2 is correct: AP's unemployment rate was 4.1% in 2023-24. 1 is wrong: the trend is reversed – India's rate fell from 6.1% (2017-18) to 3.2% (2023-24). 3 is wrong: that is the worker population ratio; the LFPR (AP 47.5%) counts the employed plus the unemployed seeking work.

st.2: Inspectors under the Act are appointed by the Central Government.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Inspectors under the Factories Act are appointed by the State Government, not the Central Government.
Both are correct: PM-JAY is the world's largest fully government-financed health assurance scheme, with ₹5 lakh cover per family per year.

st.3: PM-ABHIM, with an outlay of ₹64,180 crore, is run by the Ministry of Ayush.
st.4: The Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission was launched at Shahdol in Chhattisgarh.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: PM-ABHIM (₹64,180 crore over 6 years) is run by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, not Ayush. 4 is wrong: Shahdol is in Madhya Pradesh, not Chhattisgarh (mission launched July 2023).

st.3: Its Chairperson must be a retired judge of the Supreme Court.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: there is no such requirement for the NCM Chairperson (a judge as head is the NHRC rule); members are nominated by the Central Government for three years.

st.3: Delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion is one of its aims.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: delinking SC status from religion was a Ranganath Misra recommendation; the programme's aims are education, fair share in jobs, living conditions and prevention of communal riots.

st.3: ALIMCO is a Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: ALIMCO (1972) is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities), not Health.

st.4: The Permanent Indus Commission has one Commissioner from each country.

x: All four are correct: Kirthai-II and Sawalkote are on the Chenab, India rejected the 2026 PCA ruling, it sent a renegotiation notice in July 2026, and the PIC has one Commissioner from each country.

st.3: The third summit (2015) in New Delhi, like the first two, limited attendance to states chosen under the Banjul formula.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: unlike the first two (Banjul formula), IAFS-III (New Delhi, 2015) was open to and attended by all 54 African states.

st.1: It was set up in 1966 at the initiative of UNCTAD.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the ADB was created in 1966 at the initiative of UN-ESCAP, not UNCTAD.

st.3: The Japanese yen was the currency added to the basket in 2016.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Chinese renminbi (yuan) was added in 2016; the yen was already in the basket (dollar, euro, renminbi, yen, pound).

st.1: New START (2010) was a treaty between the USA and China.

x: Only 2 is correct: INF (1987) was a USA-USSR treaty and the US withdrew in 2019. 1 is wrong: New START was between the USA and Russia, not China (Russia suspended it in 2023).

st.2: New Articles added by amendments are numbered serially after Article 395.

x: Only 1 is correct: there are now 12 Schedules. 2 is wrong: new Articles are lettered (like 21A), so the numbering still ends at Article 395.

st.2: A validating law may simply declare a judgment void.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: a validating law cannot simply declare a judgment void; it must remove the basis of the judgment.

st.2: It provided for a Federal Public Service Commission only, with no Provincial or Joint Commissions.
st.3: It retained the Council of India with an enlarged membership.

x: Only 1 is correct: Sir Maurice Gwyer was the first CJ of the Federal Court. 2 is wrong: the Act provided for Federal, Provincial and Joint PSCs. 3 is wrong: it abolished the Council of India and gave the Secretary of State a team of advisers.

st.2: Dr B.R. Ambedkar presided over the Assembly after Rajendra Prasad.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Ambedkar chaired only the Drafting Committee and never presided over the Assembly; Sinha presided first (temporary) and Prasad was the elected President.

st.2: The original Constitution of India already contained the Ninth Schedule.

x: Only 1 is correct: the Draft had 315 Articles. 2 is wrong: the original Constitution had 395 Articles and 8 Schedules; the Ninth Schedule was added by the First Amendment (1951).

st.2: 'Begar' means forced labour for which fair wages are paid.
st.3: Under Article 23(2), the State must pay remuneration in every case of compulsory service.

x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: begar is involuntary forced labour without payment. 3 is wrong: the State may impose compulsory service for public purposes without paying in every case; it only may not discriminate on religion, race, caste or class.

st.1: It may be proclaimed only when the financial stability of the whole of India, not any part of it, is threatened.
st.2: It permits the reduction of salaries of persons serving the Union, excluding Supreme Court and High Court judges.
st.4: It has been proclaimed once, during the 1991 crisis.

x: Only 3 is correct: State Money and Financial Bills may be reserved for the President. 1 is wrong: it covers a threat to the financial stability or credit of India or any part of it. 2 is wrong: salaries may be cut for all Union servants including SC and HC judges. 4 is wrong: a Financial Emergency has never been declared.

st.2: Article 21 uses the expression 'due process of law'.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Art. 21 says 'procedure established by law' (from Japan), not 'due process of law' (an American concept); Bachan Singh (1980) upheld the death penalty in the 'rarest of rare' cases.

st.2: SEBC stands for 'Socially and Economically Backward Classes'.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: SEBC = Socially and Educationally Backward Classes, not 'Economically'.

st.2: In the absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides.
st.3: Its quorum is one-tenth of the members of the Lok Sabha alone.
st.4: A Bill is passed at a joint sitting by two-thirds of the members present and voting.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the RS Chairman never presides – after the Speaker and Deputy Speaker comes the Deputy Chairman of the RS. 3 is wrong: the quorum is one-tenth of the total members of both Houses. 4 is wrong: a simple majority of members present and voting suffices (Art. 108(4)).

st.1: Goa, Daman and Diu were made a full State by the 12th Amendment, 1962.
st.3: Sikkim became a full State by the 36th Amendment without ever having been an associate State.

x: Only 2 is correct: Pondicherry became a UT by the 14th Amendment (1962). 1 is wrong: the 12th Amendment made Goa, Daman and Diu a Union Territory, not a State. 3 is wrong: Sikkim was first an associate State (35th Amendment, 1974) before becoming the 22nd State by the 36th (1975).

st.3: A second chamber speeds up law-making.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: a second chamber causes delay and duplication; it does not speed up law-making.

st.2: A tax can be imposed with the approval of the Rajya Sabha alone.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: no tax can be imposed without the approval of the Lok Sabha.

st.1: Question Hour, supplementary questions and adjournment motions together form the 'accountability triangle', all three being provided for in the Constitution itself.
st.2: A walkout is one of the instruments of parliamentary control.
st.4: Dissolution of the House is a tool of parliamentary control.

x: Only 3 is correct: Question Hour is the most effective day-to-day vigil. 1 is wrong: these devices rest on the Rules of Procedure of the Houses, not the Constitution. 2 is wrong: a walkout is a protest, not an instrument. 4 is wrong: dissolution is an executive power; the instruments are deliberation, approval or refusal of laws, financial control and the no-confidence motion.

st.2: It is held by the Finance Secretary, Department of Expenditure, on behalf of the President.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Contingency Fund of India is held by the Finance Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, not Expenditure.

st.3: The Railway Convention Committee is a standing committee.
st.4: A Bill is referred to a Joint Committee by an order of the Speaker, without any motion in the House.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Railway Convention Committee is an ad hoc inquiry committee. 4 is wrong: a Bill goes to a Select or Joint Committee by a motion adopted in the House.

st.1: The President addresses his resignation to the Chief Justice of India.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the President addresses his resignation to the Vice-President (not the CJI), who informs the Speaker.

st.2: An ordinance is not subject to judicial review.

x: Only 1 is correct: an ordinance may be withdrawn at any time. 2 is wrong: an ordinance is subject to judicial review.

st.2: A candidate must be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
st.4: He addresses his resignation to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: a VP candidate must be qualified for the Rajya Sabha (the President for the Lok Sabha). 4 is wrong: the VP resigns to the President, not the Speaker.

st.2: Maladministration alone is a proper ground for invoking it.
st.4: The Andhra Pradesh High Court's 2020 'constitutional breakdown' observation was upheld by the Supreme Court.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: maladministration alone, intra-party disputes and ordinary law and order are improper grounds. 4 is wrong: the AP High Court's observation was stayed by the Supreme Court.

st.2: It covers only a PM or CM, and not other Ministers, held in custody for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five years or more.
st.3: Such a person can be removed from office only after being convicted by a court.

x: Only 1 is correct: it amends Articles 75, 164 and 239AA. 2 is wrong: it covers the PM, CMs and other Ministers alike. 3 is wrong: no conviction is needed – removal follows on the 31st day of continuous custody.

st.3: He presides over joint sittings of Parliament.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the AG may take part in joint sittings but does not preside over them (the Speaker does).

st.1: It gives effect to the right to a healthy environment, which Article 21 states expressly.
st.3: Besides the Principal Bench at New Delhi, it has zonal benches at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai and Jaipur.
st.4: An appeal against its order lies to the High Court concerned.

x: Only 2 is correct: Section 20 applies sustainable development, the precautionary and polluter-pays principles. 1 is wrong: the right to a healthy environment is read into Article 21 by the courts, not stated in it. 3 is wrong: there is no Jaipur bench – the zonal benches are Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai. 4 is wrong: appeals lie directly to the Supreme Court (Section 22).

st.1: It moved five subjects, including weights and measures, from the Union List to the Concurrent List.
st.3: The 'administration of justice' entry it moved covers all courts, including the High Courts.
st.4: It also moved public order and police to the Concurrent List.

x: Only 2 is correct: Entry 20A (population control and family planning). 1 is wrong: the five subjects moved from the State List, not the Union List. 3 is wrong: the entry covers all courts except the Supreme Court and the High Courts. 4 is wrong: public order and police remain in the State List.

st.1: The expression 'Union of India' includes both the States and the Union Territories.
st.4: Laws under Articles 2 and 3 that alter the First and Fourth Schedules are amendments under Article 368.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: 'Union of India' means the States only; the 'territory of India' includes States, UTs and acquired territories. 4 is wrong: Art. 4 says such laws are not deemed Art. 368 amendments.

st.2: In 2026 the Centre proposed extending the Sixth Schedule to Ladakh to safeguard its interests.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the 2026 model for Ladakh is Article 371-like safeguards instead of the Sixth Schedule.

st.2: Discretionary grants under Article 282 are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Article 282 discretionary grants are not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; Article 275 statutory grants are.

st.1: Article 280, which provides for it, is in Part XIV of the Constitution.
st.2: Article 290 also deals with the Finance Commission.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: Art. 280 is in Part XII (Part XIV is the services and PSCs). 2 is wrong: Articles 280 and 281 deal with the FC; Art. 290 is about pensions.

st.3: Tax and fiscal effort was retained as a criterion.
st.4: Contribution to GDP replaced income distance as the criterion with the highest weight.

x: 1 and 2 are correct: income distance 42.5% and population (2011) 17.5%. 3 is wrong: the 16th FC dropped tax and fiscal effort. 4 is wrong: contribution to GDP was added for the first time with only 10%; income distance still carries the highest weight.

st.1: It was constituted under C. Rangarajan.
st.3: It gave forest cover the highest weight among its criteria.

x: 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the 14th FC (constituted 2013) was chaired by Y.V. Reddy, not C. Rangarajan. 3 is wrong: forest cover carried only 7.5%; income distance (50%) had the highest weight.

st.2: Article 324 was described as a 'reservoir of power' by the Supreme Court in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Article 324 was called a 'reservoir of power' in Mohinder Singh Gill (1978), not T.N. Seshan (1995), which upheld the multi-member Commission.

st.3: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Lokpal Selection Committee is the PM, the Lok Sabha Speaker, the LoP, the CJI or a nominated judge and an eminent jurist – not the Rajya Sabha Chairman.

st.2: The Prisons Act, 1894 kept prisons with the Union Government, which alone frames prison rules.
st.3: The Model Prisons Act, 2023 prepared by the MHA is binding on all States.
st.4: The BPR&D issues binding directions on prison administration that every State must follow.

x: Only 1 is correct: prisons are Entry 4 of the State List. 2 is wrong: the 1894 Act kept prisons with the Provincial (now State) Governments. 3 is wrong: the Model Prisons Act 2023 is only a guide for States. 4 is wrong: the BPR&D only issues advisory guidelines, since prisons are a State subject.

st.2: A convict need not be informed in writing of the rejection of his mercy petition.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Court required the rejection to be communicated in writing, with 14 days' notice before execution.

All three are correct: Ministers other than the CM and MLAs are within the Lokayukta's purview, the Governor appoints on a selection committee's recommendation for 5 years, and T. Mallikarjuna Rao was appointed in Aug 2026.

st.2: The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are members of the Selection Committee.
st.3: The Search Committee consists of at least seven persons, with no reservation for SC, ST, OBC, minority or women members.

x: Only 1 is correct: the PM chairs the Selection Committee. 2 is wrong: the LoP in the Lok Sabha is a member but the Rajya Sabha Chairman is not. 3 is wrong: at least half of the (at least seven) Search Committee members must be from SC, ST, OBC, minorities or women.

st.2: It targets general government debt of 40% and Central government debt of 60% of GDP by 2025.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: it reverses the figures – general government debt is to be 60% and Central debt 40% of GDP by 2025.

st.3: Under MPLADS, works recommended by an MP are executed by the MP's own office and monitored on the eSAKSHI portal.
st.4: District and Metropolitan Planning Committees are parallel bodies outside the Constitution.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: under MPLADS the Implementing District Authority executes the works (eSAKSHI monitors them), not the MP's office. 4 is wrong: the DPC (243ZD) and MPC (243ZE) are constitutional bodies.

st.3: Ripon's resolution provided for official chairmen and nominated official majorities in local boards.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Ripon's resolution provided for non-official majorities, elected where possible, and non-official chairmen.

st.2: The 64th Amendment Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 64th Bill passed the Lok Sabha (August 1989) but was defeated in the Rajya Sabha (October 1989).

st.1: It was appointed in December 1977 by the Janata government headed by Charan Singh.
st.4: It recommended a three-tier system with the block-level Panchayat Samiti as its pivot.

x: 2 and 3 are correct: the report (August 1978, 132 recommendations) proposed Mandal Panchayats of 15,000-20,000. 1 is wrong: the Janata Prime Minister was Morarji Desai, not Charan Singh. 4 is wrong: Ashok Mehta recommended a two-tier system (Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat), with the district as the pivot.

st.4: The national institute NIRDPR is located in Vijayawada.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: NIRDPR is in Hyderabad, not Vijayawada.

st.2: Article 243G deals with the finances of Panchayats.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Article 243G deals with the powers and responsibilities of Panchayats (Eleventh Schedule); finances and taxes are under Article 243H.

st.2: The State Finance Commission appoints the State Election Commissioner.
st.3: Under Article 243H Panchayats may levy, collect and appropriate taxes on their own, without any authorisation by the State Legislature.
st.4: The intermediate tier has the main own-tax domain, such as property tax.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the Governor, not the SFC, appoints the State Election Commissioner. 3 is wrong: under Art. 243H Panchayats tax only as the State Legislature authorises by law. 4 is wrong: the Gram Panchayat has the main own taxes (house/property tax).

st.1: The intermediate tier in Andhra Pradesh is the Panchayat Samiti, not the Mandal Parishad.
st.3: In Andhra Pradesh the Sarpanch of a Gram Panchayat is elected indirectly by the ward members.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: AP's intermediate tier is the Mandal Parishad, not the Panchayat Samiti. 3 is wrong: in AP the Sarpanch is elected directly by the voters.

st.2: Reservation for Backward Classes in local bodies is compulsory in every State.
st.3: The minimum age of 21 years applies to Panchayat elections only, and not to Municipal elections.
st.4: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993, a day now observed as National Voters' Day.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: BC reservation is left to the States. 3 is wrong: the minimum age of 21 applies to both Panchayat and Municipal elections. 4 is wrong: 24 April (1993) is observed as National Panchayati Raj Day; National Voters' Day is 25 January.

st.2: It also reserves one-third of seats for women in the Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils.
st.3: It provides an OBC sub-quota within the women's reservation.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils are not covered. 3 is wrong: there is no OBC sub-quota.

st.2: After the first notification, the President can include or exclude a tribe by a fresh public notification.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: under Art. 342(2) later inclusion or exclusion is only by Parliament by law, not by a fresh Presidential notification.

st.1: In July 1991 the rupee was made fully convertible on the capital account.
st.3: Interest-rate deregulation followed the Tarapore Committee.

x: Only 2 is correct: tax cuts followed the Chelliah Committee. 1 is wrong: July 1991 saw a devaluation; the rupee has never been fully capital-account convertible. 3 is wrong: interest deregulation followed the Narasimham Committee; Tarapore dealt with capital account convertibility.

st.1: The AITUC, India's oldest central trade union, was founded under the Trade Unions Act, 1926.
st.3: The BMS was founded in 1955 as the labour wing of the Congress.

x: Only 2 is correct: INTUC (1947). 1 is wrong: the AITUC (1920, N.M. Joshi) predates the Trade Unions Act, 1926. 3 is wrong: the BMS (1955) is linked to the Sangh Parivar; INTUC is the Congress's labour wing.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh was placed among the 'Fast Movers' among coastal States in LEADS 2023.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh was an 'Achiever', not a 'Fast Mover', in LEADS 2023.

st.2: PMSBY covers death from any cause, including illness.
st.3: PMSBY provides an old-age pension.

x: Only 1 is correct: PMJJBY is one-year renewable term life insurance. 2 is wrong: PMSBY covers only accidental death and disability (death from any cause is PMJJBY). 3 is wrong: PMSBY is not a pension scheme.

st.1: It was launched on 15 August 1995 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
st.2: It fulfils the directive in Article 43 of the Constitution.
st.4: Its old-age pension had kept its real value by May 2026, being indexed to inflation.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: NSAP is under the Ministry of Rural Development. 2 is wrong: it fulfils Article 41, not Article 43. 4 is wrong: the pension is not indexed – by May 2026 it had lost nearly half its real value.

st.2: Saubhagya (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana, 2017) is a scheme of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Saubhagya is a scheme of the Ministry of Power, not MNRE.
All three are correct: FD was 4.8% in FY25 against 4.9% budgeted, S&P upgraded India from BBB- to BBB, and the Survey flagged State revenue deficits and unconditional cash transfers.

st.3: The Centre's gross tax revenue recorded its highest growth (17.9%) in 2016-17, the year GST was introduced.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 17.9% growth came in 2016-17, but GST was introduced only on 1 July 2017 (2017-18).

st.2: Of Andhra Pradesh's 175 Assembly seats, 29 are reserved for Scheduled Tribes and 7 for Scheduled Castes.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: it swaps the categories – of AP's 175 seats, 29 are SC and 7 are ST.

st.2: Section 93 requires the Centre to take the Thirteenth Schedule measures within ten years.

x: All three are correct: Sec 89 extended the KWDT's term, Sec 93 gives ten years for the Thirteenth Schedule measures, and Sec 90 made Polavaram a national project.

st.1: GDP deflator = real GDP ÷ nominal GDP × 100.
st.2: It is regarded as the most comprehensive measure of inflation as it covers only a fixed basket of goods and services.

x: Only 3 is correct: a rising deflator means falling purchasing power. 1 is wrong: GDP deflator = nominal ÷ real GDP × 100. 2 is wrong: it covers all goods and services in GDP, unlike the fixed baskets of WPI/CPI.

st.2: Gig workers form a separate category in the Periodic Labour Force Survey.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: gig workers (about 2% of the 61.6 crore workforce) are not yet a separate PLFS category.

st.2: Jobless growth is likelier when growth is led by labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and construction.
st.3: High growth of labour-intensive manufacturing is a cause of unemployment.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: jobless growth is likelier with capital-intensive sectors such as IT and finance. 3 is wrong: labour-intensive manufacturing creates jobs; it is not a cause of unemployment.

st.3: SVAMITVA drone maps, under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, can give panchayats a property-tax baseline.
st.4: The Smart Cities Mission rewards cities for property-tax reform and municipal bonds.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: SVAMITVA is a scheme of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, not Housing and Urban Affairs. 4 is wrong: it is AMRUT 2.0, not the Smart Cities Mission, that rewards property-tax reform and municipal bonds.

st.2: NPCI is a statutory body created by the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
st.3: The National Financial Switch (NFS) was designed and launched by NPCI in 2004.

x: Only 1 is correct: NPCI was set up by the RBI and the IBA. 2 is wrong: NPCI is a not-for-profit company authorised under the PSS Act, 2007, not a statutory body created by it. 3 is wrong: NFS was launched in 2004 by the RBI's IDRBT; NPCI (December 2008) took it over in 2009.

st.1: The Board for Financial Supervision was set up in 1994 under the chairmanship of the Finance Minister.
st.2: The Tarapore Committee (1997; 2006) scrutinised applications for new bank licences.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: the BFS (1994) is chaired by the RBI Governor, not the Finance Minister. 2 is wrong: the Tarapore Committee dealt with capital account convertibility; new bank licences were scrutinised by the Bimal Jalan panel.

st.2: Complaints above a fixed amount fall outside it.

x: Only 1 is correct: RB-IOS 2026 ('One Nation One Ombudsman') began on 1 July 2026. 2 is wrong: it puts no cap on the amount of a complaint.

st.1: The fiscal deficit is a part of monetary policy, not fiscal policy.
st.4: 'Fiscal dominance' refers to the RBI's control over the Government's borrowing programme.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the fiscal deficit belongs to fiscal policy. 4 is wrong: fiscal dominance means heavy Government borrowing pressing on money supply and inflation, not RBI control over borrowing.

st.2: In May 2026, Andhra Pradesh's retail inflation (3.9%) was below the national rate (4.9%).

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: it was the reverse – AP's retail inflation was 4.9% against the national 3.9%.

st.4: Sahakar Sarathi, the shared-services entity for cooperatives, was set up by SIDBI.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: Sahakar Sarathi is NABARD's shared-services entity, approved by the RBI – not SIDBI's.

st.2: Microfinance loans must be backed by collateral.

x: Only 1 is correct: NBFC-MFIs must hold at least 75% of assets in microfinance loans. 2 is wrong: microfinance loans are collateral-free.

st.3: Under GST 2.0, about 99% of items of the old 12% slab moved to 18%.
st.4: Under GST 2.0, about 90% of items of the old 28% slab moved to 40%.

st.1: Seed Replacement Rate is the percentage of a crop's area sown with farm-saved seed rather than certified/quality seed.
